category_title: Students who engage in high social interaction but require frequent off-task redirection
minimal_context: The student is working in a mixed-age group of two to three peers on a collaborative project in a high school social studies classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please get into your groups of two or three and start working on your collaborative social studies project.

STUDENT: Hey guys! It's so great to be in a group with you. Did you see that new movie that came out this weekend?

TUTOR: Let's try to look at the assignment.

STUDENT: Yeah, we will in a second. I'm just easily distracted today. But seriously, the ending of that movie was crazy, right?

TUTOR: Keep trying to work on the project.

STUDENT: I'm trying, but I just have a total lack of focuses right now. Anyway, what are you guys doing after school today?

options.A: Instruct the student to take out paper and individually write a detailed retelling of the social studies topic from beginning to end.
options.B: Walk around the classroom, conference with the students, and sit in on the groups to observe and record their interactions during the project.
options.C: Leave the group completely free to choose any format and materials they like to complete the collaborative social studies project during the session.
options.D: Have the group use a digital mind-mapping tool to organize their research and structure their project by creating color-coded nodes with text and images.
